purpose: Preserve the operator's full non-AI photo, timeline, motion, compositing and supporting audio production scope while evaluating reusable Rust code and identifying required proofs. This file neither approves implementation nor certifies parity.

scope_preservation.requirement: Lightroom and Camera Raw class catalogue, development, tethering and output workflows are included; Adobe AI implementation is excluded by operator instruction.
Professional Premiere class timeline editing, After Effects class animation/compositing/VFX and Media Encoder class delivery workflows are included.
Supporting Audition class audio editing, restoration, mixing and delivery are mapped so picture workflows do not end at a nominal video editor.

Native Rust engines are preferred. An existing Rust implementation may be forked or adapted after source, dependency, fidelity and target-platform proof. Rust bindings around a native C/C++ engine are identified as adapters.
One Studio crate containing all engines is a failed architecture. Reuse canonical owners across document domains and avoid a default dependency closure that recompiles every codec, GUI and engine.

A Handshake native document carries interchangeable photo, raster, vector, layout, design, sequence and composition workflows. Adobe files open through conversion with truthful editable-fidelity and unsupported-feature reports.

Studio begins as independent assets without changing the active Handshake kernel build; each future crate exposes integration seams for Flight Recorder/EventLedger, internal diagnostics, Palmistry and Argus.

A shared desktop panel/control/viewport asset is expanded through typed features and bindings before a near-identical asset is created. Human and model manuals, quiet operation, parallel agent edits and visual inspection apply to every domain.
Existing RAW, video, animation and compositing prep is carried forward. This repass does not replace prep or interpret an upstream project's scope exclusions as permission to reduce Handshake scope.

local_authority_evidence.fact: Resolver selects active v02.206 indexed Master Spec; the Product Reference is navigation only.
Manifest is the indexed spec hash authority; INDEX.json is the module resolver.
Section 14.25 explicitly supersedes and inverts the early STU-OVR-015 NLE exclusion. Studio owns interactive sequence editing; engine.director consumes Studio sequences.

StudioSequence is a member of the unified StudioDocument; stored time is integer ticks at 254016000000 per second. Broadcast rates use canonical 1001-denominator forms; decimal legacy imports normalize explicitly.

Shipping codec choices, caption coverage and the detailed Director input API still require decisions. Every editing control and outcome must be typed, model-steerable, Argus-inspectable and documented.
Animation prep already defines composition/layer models, property trees, exact time, keyframes, graph editor, time remap, expressions, text animators, shapes, scripting and render output.

Layer document model is normative; a node document surface remains an open decision. The addressable per-frame render dependency graph is required and does not authorize replacing the layer document model.

Shared shell supplies composition/sequence/source/footage/layer/catalogue and other viewport kinds; photo layouts are marked extrapolated and need runtime capture. ParamSpec and UiDescriptor provide shared controls, temporal writes and manuals.
Business Flight Recorder/EventLedger, internal diagnostics and external Palmistry are separate surfaces with allowlisted diagnostic payloads.
Stable Argus inspect/click/set_value/screenshot routes and agent_label attribution are required. Missing in-scope Argus paths block proof; model/human manuals must reflect actual behavior.
Each MT has one owning module; dependency and compile boundaries are deliberate; mechanics belong to the lowest canonical reusable owner.

Current storage authority is SurrealDB/EventLedger and expressly forbids SQLite import, connectivity, reconciliation, fixtures and compatibility paths. A pure Rust SQLite reader remains a SQLite import path.

Mechanical Director rendering/transcode/extract/supercut contracts provide the later consumer seam; current numeric fps contracts need explicit mapping from exact Studio time, not implicit float conversion.
Existing feature research is preserved as reference. Historic advice against a new native format does not override the live operator's request for one.

Inspected existing RAW interop plan carries forward immutable RAW/develop graph, Bayer/X-Trans/DNG decode, filmstrip and shared parameter controls; SurrealDB/EventLedger owns state and XMP is transport, not authority.

Actual MCP request wire consumes top-level client_session_id with a bounded ASCII identity and connection-session fallback. agent_label is not an inspected implemented alias; HBR label wording and wire need reconciliation before manuals/examples.

Current spec expressly forbids a bespoke native file-on-disk format; the operator-requested portable native container therefore needs an approved exact amendment before implementation. Existing import/edit-preserve/export/round-trip contracts, fixtures and explicit color/units/actor events must remain preserved.

Import supports preview choices, smart previews, naming, metadata and development settings.
Tethered capture/live view is a camera-specific workflow requiring compatibility and disconnect handling.
Development combines global/local controls, presets, snapshots/history, filmstrip, before/after and optics.
RAW/DNG development retains process/profile interpretation as distinct from raster editing.
Panorama and bracketed HDR panorama are non-AI production requirements with projection, alignment and preview choices.
Official workflow index provides the vendor baseline for media organization, editing, monitors, audio, graphics, color and delivery; index presence is not a fidelity proof.
Multicam source/target sequences, angle monitoring, live switching and subsequent trimming must survive timeline edits.
Source/log interpretation, sequence working space, tone mapping, monitoring and export color are separate decisions.
Proxy use for editing must be distinguished from explicit proxy/preview export; original media is the normal delivery source.
Film/TV practice includes offline dailies, media identity, turnover, conform and delivery. Linked full guide PDF was discovered but was not inspected in this pass.

AAF turnover distinguishes handles, separate/embedded media, BWF channel breakout and unsupported constructs. Vendor documentation reports an embedded-media size constraint on both Windows Intel and Arm; large jobs need explicit separate-media proof.
Delivery includes mastering/interchange/image-sequence formats beyond a single compressed MP4.
Animation/compositing reference includes keyframes, property graphs, tracking, masks, expressions, 3D and render output.
ICC and OCIO/ACES workflows separate input, working, display-preview and output transforms, with precision/HDR requirements.
Shape/mask path interpolation, manual corrections and temporal consistency remain required independently of AI tools.
AEP is binary; AEPX contains XML and encoded binary information. Collecting a project preserves asset relationships; XML appearance alone does not establish a complete editable importer.
Relink, reload, interpret, reduce and consolidate must maintain footage identity and composition dependencies.
Delivery uses queues, multiple outputs, settings/presets, watch folders, progress, cancellation and distinct completion/failure states while editing continues.
Render jobs, presets, progress and watch-folder operations are professional automation surfaces; vendor API is public beta, not a Handshake dependency.
Dialogue/music/SFX/ambience workflows combine loudness and conventional DSP repairs; algorithms require independent audio proof.
Spectral frequency selection exposes time/frequency/amplitude information that waveform-only editing cannot replace.
Multitrack sessions, nondestructive mixer/effect racks and batch loudness delivery support picture production.

Native SESX is XML-based session state referencing audio/video files, envelopes and effects; sample rate, precision and channel/mix layout matter. XML readability is not a complete semantic importer proof.

Native SESX retains session state; FCP XML interchange excludes overlapping clips, effects/EQ, most automation, routing/sends/buses and stereo channel information. Native session conversion cannot be silently replaced by that interchange.

Conventional restoration combines manual spectral selection, noise prints and realtime/offline processing; excessive reduction can introduce audible artifacts, requiring listening and independent signal checks.
Pure Rust audio demux/decode/metadata candidate; MPL-2.0, not a DAW or a universal video codec engine.
Rust AV1 encoder candidate with BSD-2-Clause licensing and optional architecture-specific assembly; still needs profile/speed/quality and ARM/x64 packaging proof.
Rust plugins use the native GStreamer core through bindings; identify as an optional native-runtime adapter, not a pure Rust replacement engine.
Apache-2.0 editorial timeline interchange reference with C++/Python implementation; not the native Studio document or an effect renderer.
Native OpenColorIO processing API is a reference oracle or optional adapter. A Rust wrapper does not make its C++ engine native Rust.
Composable Rust DSP fundamentals; does not supply complete restoration/mixing/editor parity.
Rust OS audio-device I/O candidate; device behavior and clocking remain platform-specific, separate from the DSP model.

Recent issue reports include GPU-memory/texture limits, view lag, shape/mask interactions, platform input and UI behavior. A test/file claim is not an ARM/x64 runtime proof in this repass.

source_findings.finding: Mixer separates clips/trim/inserts/sends/fader/pan/buses/main with no-allocation steady-state design. Fixed channel limits and third-party plugin control-thread behavior must become explicit capabilities.
CPAL playback swaps session snapshots, uses atomics for meters and a device-less silent clock fallback. Expose silent/offline and actual hardware playback separately.
VST3 host separates unsafe FFI/libloading from engine owners. This is an isolation pattern, not proof of plugin fidelity or ARM/x64 editor-window behavior.
Sources decoding into memory and missing disk streaming limit long sessions; platform/runtime and plugin-editor gaps remain. No claim of complete Audition spectral/session parity.

proposed_modular_owners.naming: The operator invited Handshake-themed naming; parent deliberates names against existing Studio law. This map names responsibilities only and does not establish new product taxonomy.

rules.proposal: Foundational document types, exact time, geometry, color identities, asset references and command/diagnostic contracts have lightweight canonical owners. No database, GUI, OS codec or huge rendering dependency belongs in these types.

RAW/photo compute, image/raster compute, timeline/edit compute, animation evaluation, compositor render planning, audio DSP/mix and delivery are separate owners. Reuse time/color/mask/shape/text/parameter mechanisms rather than duplicating each craft foundation.

Each codec/demux/encoder and hardware/native plugin/device adapter is an explicit leaf; optional heavy dependencies compile only for requested capabilities. A codecs-all default hub is not an acceptable replacement for a single Studio crate.
SurrealDB/EventLedger repository adapters, kernel diagnostics/FR/Palmistry bridges and Argus host bridges depend on domain contracts; pure engines must not import kernel storage, .GOV or GUI.
Shared desktop assets bind typed trees/media tables, inspectors, timelines/curve editors, swatches/menus and viewports. Domain presenters add descriptors and modes; they do not fork the assets.

owns: encoders and pure format conversion leaves
Flight Recorder and internal diagnostic/Palmistry bridge
neutral ParamSpec/UiDescriptor and immutable descriptor snapshot binding
domain-specific descriptor and viewport content providers
nodes.provider_note: Each selected presenter depends only on its neutral domain contract and selected implementation ports; this grouping is not an all-engine Cargo package or unconditional dependency on every media engine.

proposed_modular_owners.dag_note: This is a responsibility/dependency proposal, not a Cargo manifest. Shared raster/vector/text/color owners are jointly deliberated with engineering and UI; remove cycles and accidental all-feature fan-in before approving real crate edges. Domain IDs preserve names already specified by Studio.
proposed_modular_owners.build_proof: Before adopting forks, inventory actual Cargo edges/features/MSRV/native build scripts and compare with current Handshake dependencies. Then define approved owner-scoped warm compile/relink budgets and canonical external target/cache paths per HBR; no builds were authorized or run in this research lane.

native_document_media_proposal.existing_law: STU-VID-010 already embeds sequences/compositions/artboards/pages in StudioDocument. STU-IO-001 currently forbids a bespoke on-disk container: the live operator request requires an exact approved amendment, not a claim that the new format is already permitted. A file container serializes the document; it does not replace authoritative runtime storage, source-format import/edit-preserve/export/round-trip commitments, or merge all engines into one crate.

conversion_rules.proposal: Keep original Adobe source read-only; conversion stages a complete report before replacing or committing the native document. Preserve opaque unsupported payloads and source handles when practical.

Represent editable-exact, editable-approximate, baked-preview, unsupported-retained, blocked-policy and failed outcomes separately. A file opening or a flattened image is not complete editable fidelity.

Require per-format/version fixtures for PSD/PSB/AI/INDD/IDML/PRPROJ/AEP/AEPX/LRCAT/SESX and supporting presets/XMP/session formats. Engineering owns non-media importer details; AEPX XML, editorial XML/AAF or an XMP sidecar does not substitute for the native project/catalogue/session requested.
An unknown codec/profile/plugin/transform or missing source remains visible and recoverable. Never silently bake/omit/replace it while certifying editable parity.

Version importers and native migrations independently, bound decompression/parser resources, validate paths and retain source identity so interrupted/malformed imports cannot corrupt originals or existing documents.

integration_and_model_contracts.boundary: Studio owns interactive edit commands and document time; Director is a consumer of a validated immutable sequence/composition render plan.
proposal: Consumer input carries document revision, StudioSequence ID, exact tick interval, canonical rational frame rate, asset handles, shared render/color/audio plan and explicit output policy
Map to current Director sandbox/artifact/proc.exec limits through a kernel bridge, not an engine dependency on kernel
Reject unsupported time/profile/effect mappings before rendering; do not reduce exact Studio time to unqualified float fps
Return artifact identity, timing/color/audio metadata, diagnostics and cancellation/failure receipts
Do not claim this detailed API is implemented: current product grep/engine config inspection did not establish an active Director consumer implementation
Every field/slider/menu/swatch/track/clip/keyframe/mask/viewport binds a stable author_id and typed command/ParamSpec route
Shared asset descriptors expose available feature modes; domain code extends a canonical asset before introducing a near-identical one

Requests use the approved attributed client field and independent client view/selection/playhead context plus base document/object revision; current MCP consumes client_session_id, while agent_label in HBR prose is an unresolved name/alias contract
Attribution/view labels are not authorization; every source/retained blob/intermediate/preview/inspect/capture uses the authenticated actor's current grants and revocation state
Inspect returns canonical object/property state, effective defaults, support status, dependencies, conflict/error and operation receipt

Screenshot carries document revision, render revision, sequence/composition/layer ID, exact ticks/frame/rational rate, DPI/viewport geometry/zoom-pan-rotation, original-proxy identity, display/output transform and pending/stale state
Headless/quiet captures expose final and intermediate rendered outcomes; human focus and keyboard state remain unchanged
Pixel comparison, color fidelity, encoded output and audible/sample correctness are separate gates; no screenshot replaces the latter proofs

Each owner reports typed decode/profile/eval/render/audio/export failures with operation correlation and bounded reproducible state; document object IDs/context are emitted only in the explicitly owning granted schema, not implicitly into a shared diagnostic ring
Business edits/exports/conversions produce FR/EventLedger receipts; allowlisted timings/device/GPU/cache/queue/underrun/retry go to internal diagnostics
Palmistry receives only approved allowlisted diagnostic fields and versions; document text, pixels, filenames/source content are not implicitly exported
Capture revision/timing/feature support and fallback identity so a no-context model can reproduce a failure
Expose GPU loss, allocation/resource exhaustion, device disconnect, parser/profile failure and oracle unavailable states; absence of a crash is not success
Human and model manuals derive from the same actual command/parameter/UiDescriptor registry
Explain purpose, input/output, native conversion fidelity classes, navigation, exact time/source/color interpretation and safe recovery
Include findable primitives/APIs, supported profiles/features and limitations for each owner
Document parallel edit/conflict/capture and quiet job operation with attributable examples
Manual capability claims are checked against actual engine/parser/render proof, not upstream checklist counts

blockers_and_risks.impact: Requested full Lightroom .lrcat conversion cannot be implemented under the unchanged express no-SQLite rule.
blockers_and_risks.mitigation: Preserve requirement; parent proposes a narrow, approved read-only vendor-format importer exception with quarantined parsing, no SQLite runtime/storage authority, retained source and explicit conversion receipts. Do not implement until authority changes. XMP support does not close this requirement.
blockers_and_risks.next_proof: Inspect approved current authority/spec change and importer packet scope before any .lrcat reader or SQLite fixture is added.

blockers_and_risks.impact: Inspected craft sources do not establish native PRPROJ/AEP/AEPX complete editable import. Native vendor formats and plugin state are a hard engineering/research requirement.
blockers_and_risks.mitigation: Dedicated importer owners, versioned feature inventory, source-retaining typed outcomes and independent vendor reopen/reference comparisons; unsupported features block an exact editable-fidelity claim.
blockers_and_risks.next_proof: Pin and inspect actual parser source/spec and fixtures for each requested native format, then validate a production sample with source feature counts and rendered/property comparisons.

blockers_and_risks.impact: Native Rust source is not a universal codec/RAW implementation; chroma/bit-depth/interlace/VFR/damage/camera RAW and platform encode gaps remain.
blockers_and_risks.mitigation: Declare exact supported profiles and explicit optional adapter choices; keep leaves isolated; preserve full professional scope while staging named gaps. Source/dependency/license inventory is required before shipping codec selection.
blockers_and_risks.next_proof: Mandatory camera/phone/RAW/HDR/interlace/damaged corpus with independent decode/encode metadata oracles on ARM and x64.

blockers_and_risks.impact: JPEG-fitted/neutral camera color and identity fallback for unsupported color transforms can produce plausible incorrect output.
blockers_and_risks.mitigation: Canonical calibrated color owner; typed supported/unverified/unsupported status; required precision/input-working-display-output plans; block certified final output when transform fidelity is unknown.
blockers_and_risks.next_proof: Measured camera/lens/profile charts, ICC/OCIO transform corpus, HDR/alpha/print reference renders and encoded metadata.

blockers_and_risks.impact: Expression failure can silently return a base property; cycles/expensive scripts can stall renders or yield wrong revisions.
blockers_and_risks.mitigation: Typed errors and dependency/cycle/resource budgets; explicit preview fallback state and block certified final output without a receipted policy.
blockers_and_risks.next_proof: Error, cyclic dependency, deterministic random, time remap, recursion/resource and vendor property/render fixtures.

blockers_and_risks.impact: Self-roundtrip, source tests that silently skip and sparse screenshots can give a false parity verdict.
blockers_and_risks.mitigation: Independent required oracles and corpus identity; unavailable prerequisites return BLOCKED. Report feature presence, behavior fidelity, visual fidelity, performance and interoperability separately.
blockers_and_risks.next_proof: Demonstrate the gate fails when oracle/corpus is absent and passes only after exact outputs are independently compared.

blockers_and_risks.impact: Multiple craft forks or all-codec hubs recreate a monolithic rebuild closure and duplicate common owners.
blockers_and_risks.mitigation: Select one canonical time/color/raster/path/text/control/document owner; feature-gate codec/platform leaves and keep kernel/UI/storage out of compute crates.
blockers_and_risks.next_proof: Actual Cargo graph and incremental edit-to-compile/relink measurements mapped to approved owner budgets, using canonical external artifact/cache roots.

blockers_and_risks.impact: Upstream platform builds or macOS-centered development do not establish ARM Surface development or Windows x64 production behavior.
blockers_and_risks.mitigation: Separate architecture/platform capability probes and runtime lanes, generic CPU fallback with truthful diagnostics, optional hardware/plugin leaf boundaries and shared semantic Argus controls.
blockers_and_risks.next_proof: ARM and x64 cold/warm startup, media-device/render/export, DPI/keyboard/touch/accessibility/Argus and resource-recovery workflows.

blockers_and_risks.impact: RAM-decoded sources, fixed channel limits and silent device fallback cannot establish long multichannel production audio workflows.
blockers_and_risks.mitigation: Stream/cache sources behind immutable sessions, enforce callback safety and explicit layout/device/silent state; keep plugin work off real-time thread.
blockers_and_risks.next_proof: Long-source memory/streaming, audio-callback allocation/lock, device loss, clock drift/channel routing and independent loudness/sample-count proof.

blockers_and_risks.impact: Forked panels and GUI-only operations fragment the desktop workflow and prevent agents from judging changes.
blockers_and_risks.mitigation: Shared assets with typed domain bindings and feature introspection; extend existing asset before duplication; stable Argus routes and truthful dual manuals; separate client contexts.
blockers_and_risks.next_proof: Cross-domain human and concurrent agent workflow exercising the same panel/control assets plus rendered outcomes at recorded revisions.

deliberation_summary.engineering: Coordinate one canonical time/color/geometry/path/text/raster/format foundation; engine leaves and optional native adapters must stay separate from storage/kernel/UI. Engineering owns PhotoCraft/VectorCraft/DesignCraft deeper audits; media owns FilmCraft/LightCraft/EffectCraft and supporting audio. Peer review requested explicit catalogue semantics, spectral/streamed audio, immutable delivery ownership, foundation time contracts instead of Motion-to-NLE fan-in, and incremental-versus-sccache lane selection; engineering reported scoped proposal corrections, to be inspected by parent during final consolidation.
deliberation_summary.ui: Shared timeline/keyframes/curves, media table/tree, tagged property inspector, viewport overlays/hit targets and mask/transform mechanics can bind domain modes. Snapshot metadata must include exact time/source/profile/revision identity; visual pixel gates are distinct from color, audio and encoded-output proof.
deliberation_summary.parent: Preserve later 14.25/14.26/14.27 law and existing prep; consolidate narrow decisions and reference artifacts before approving independent Studio assets. Final themed names, native format shape and implementation packets remain parent/operator deliberation outcomes.
